headline: Modeling choices alter conclusions drawn from gene regulatory network analyses
label: Model Choice In Gene Regulation
summary: Benchmark rankings, feature importance, and Boolean control outcomes each depend on analytic choices, motivating comparative evaluation before adoption.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these three preprints is that analytic choices shape the conclusions drawn from regulatory and genomic data. One study introduces a diagnostic framework that quantifies ranking reversals across evaluation protocol axes in single-cell GRN inference benchmarks. A second proposes asymmetric Shapley values as an importance metric for high-dimensional genomic features in mixed-dimensional clinical prediction. A third surveys Boolean network control problems, offering a taxonomy and a framework that compares tool solutions, along with a mutation co-occurrence score for prioritization. These items do not share a single method. What is new is explicit attention to how evaluation protocol, importance attribution, and problem formulation alter outcomes, favoring comparative evaluation before adoption.
